legend: Low-power view showing invasive epithelial islands with cribriform morphology.
Invasive epithelial islands with cribriform morphology have an ovoid or angular outline and are set within a desmoplastic stroma.

Invasive epithelial islands containing well-defined, rounded spaces, similar in appearance to cribriform-type ductal carcinoma in situ. The islands comprise multilayered epithelial cells of small to intermediate size forming secondary glandular structures lined by cuboidal to columnar cells. Apical secretions are sometimes present, and the spaces may contain mucinous secretions with or without calcification. Mitotic activity is sparse and there is no substantial nuclear atypia.

Invasive cribriform carcinoma with irregular cribriform islands within desmoplastic stroma. A few angulated tubules are seen among the invading cribriform nests. Focal cribriform DCIS with necrosis is also noted.
